title: Lab Exhaust Flow Calculator
description: Three lab exhaust challenges: from given contaminated, bypass and entrained flows, type the fan flow, total flow and contaminated share, then see every stream on a stack diagram. Explore mode adds sliders for the three given flows.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: contaminated air
bypass flow
bypass air plenum
entrained flow
fan flow
lab exhaust total flow
plume dilution

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Lab exhaust fan flow, total flow and plume dilution
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the fan flow, the lab exhaust total flow and the contaminated share of the plume from given contaminated, bypass and entrained flows, matching the model values exactly on at least 3 of 3 challenges.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); per-value verdicts, feedback, each new challenge and the Explore summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; streams are labelled by name and value, and fresh-air streams are dashed; Enter checks and goes on; answer boxes, buttons and sliders are reachable with Tab.

controls.label: Share (%)
controls.purpose: Contaminated share of the plume, within 1 percentage point

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Check all three values (Enter); two attempts

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset the three challenges and the score

rules: Flows must equal the model values exactly; the share is correct within 1 percentage point
Two attempts per challenge; a challenge is correct only when all three values are correct
Share is 'not defined' and no plume is drawn when the total flow is 0
Explore mode notes once that fan flow stays constant when contaminated air falls and bypass rises by the same amount
assumptions: Entrained flow is treated as an independent input for practice
limitations: In a real fan, entrained flow depends on the fan flow and nozzle design and comes from the manufacturer's rating

sources: Stream names and joining order: FanPedia pp. 4 and 6 (lab exhaust diagrams) and p. 138 (bypass dampers)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit numbers before the diagram fills in, then explore the same relationships with sliders
keyQuestions: Which streams pass through the impeller?
Why is the fan selected on contaminated plus bypass flow?
How does the bypass damper keep fan flow steady as sashes close?
commonMisconceptions: Entrained air passes through the fan, so the fan must be sized for total flow
Bypass air is wasted air that does not help dilution
When fume hood exhaust drops, the fan flow must drop too
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 with all three values correct on the first attempt.
